A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, numerical comparisons and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian, ShapeNet and MCMC experiments in Section 6, plus repulsion-strength experiments in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Section 6 and the supplementary repulsion experiments, now in Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The importance-sampling estimator, three DPP constructions and spherical repulsion procedure remain unchanged. New Algorithms 2–5 document existing comparison methods; they do not establish a change to the procedures actually evaluated.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gaussian examples in dimensions 2, 10 and 20, the same two ShapeNet pairs, banana-target MCMC examples in dimensions 10 and 30, and the same appendix integration scenarios. Newly cited applications are not additional experiments.

E2.justification: The experiment-specific comparator sets in Figures 3, 5, 7 and 8 are unchanged, including the same applicable control-variate, DPP, repelled, UnifOrtho and randomized-grid methods. The four HMC/NUTS variants also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, projection budgets, reference integrations and harmonic-degree settings match. For example, both MCMC experiments use 1,000 projection directions and 10,000 reference samples. The added pseudocode does not establish revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: The spectral-profile analysis in Figure 6, integrand heatmaps in Figure 9 and repulsion-strength studies in Figures 10–12 are retained. Moving the latter appendix sections from A.3–A.4 to A.4–A.5 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 realizations for the Gaussian experiments, 1,000 for the MCMC quadrature comparisons and 100 for the appendix sensitivity experiments. Gaussian and chi-square confidence intervals, Bonferroni corrections and the single-MCMC-history qualification are unchanged.

E6.justification: The plotted results, numerical entries and reported rankings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Figure 8 retains the UnifOrtho estimate 0.0638 ± 0.0003 for regular NUTS at T = 10,000 in dimension 30.

T1.justification: Proposition 4 and the DPP limit results are retained. v2 explicitly states basis independence of the spectral energies and adds algebraic estimator formulas in Appendix A.3. The new SHCV projector and single-control-variate coefficient contain inconsistencies with the retained least-squares formulation in Equation 7.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain the same: benchmark repulsive quadratures and explain UnifOrtho through its variance. Both versions recommend randomized quasi-Monte Carlo in low dimensions and UnifOrtho in higher dimensions.

C2.justification: v2 more explicitly separates sampling error from quadrature error, distinguishes integration with easily sampled targets from adaptive MCMC, and states that its observations apply independently of the downstream ML task. Appendix A.3 also explains that SHCV quadrature weights are independent of the integrand.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project implementation link and pseudocode for HKPV sampling, SHCV, a single-control-variate estimator and Haar sampling. These supplement existing mathematical descriptions and the retained importance-sampling algorithm, rather than document new experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds six cited works covering texture synthesis, autoencoders, differential privacy, manifold flows, Wang–Landau sampling and self-repulsive dynamics. Sections 1–2 broaden application context and clarify positioning relative to repulsive MCMC without redefining the main novelty.

P1.justification: Localized additions expand the introduction, background, harmonic explanations and discussion, and summarize expected convergence rates before the experiments. The contents list is removed and a pseudocode appendix subsection is inserted; most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a journal template throughout, changing page geometry, typography, the title and author block, running headers and figure sizing and placement. Figures 7 and 8 move onto separate pages, and four algorithm displays are added. The original twelve figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves explanation and adds implementation access information, while retaining the empirical evidence and main theorem. However, new Algorithm 3 constructs an s-by-s projector from H = Phi^T Phi and uses it in an N-dimensional expression, while Algorithm 4 divides its regression coefficient by integrand variance rather than control-variate variance, conflicting with Equation 7. These errors weaken the added reproducibility guidance. The PDFs leave these inconsistencies unresolved, so the benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
